question: What operational Lead Quality threshold should Growth use, and how should Inventory Availability be expressed explicitly as a point-in-time probability component?
hypothesis: A stage-relative capacity threshold can preserve ranking lift while materially improving recall, and a temporally calibrated availability probability can be estimated from backward-as-of inventory state without future leakage.
primary_change: freeze an operational capacity/threshold policy and formalize P(availability)
secondary_changes: add a 30-day availability target for validation
use expanding temporal calibration with a 30-day maturation purge

scoring_time.stage: T0/T1/T2 for threshold policy; inquiry time for availability calibration
scoring_time.timestamp_definition: same score_time as Modelo 3; availability calibration uses inquiries.inquiry_at

availability.event: spot is available now or is observed available in a snapshot within 30 days
availability.censoring: currently-unavailable rows without any future snapshot inside the 30-day window are excluded

population.availability: inquiry/spot events with a backward-as-of snapshot and an observable 30-day availability label

validation.lead_quality: existing 4-fold temporal OOF predictions; capacity metrics computed inside fold and stage
validation.availability: 4-fold expanding chronological validation with label_mature_at < test_start purge

decision_rule.threshold: choose the smallest operational capacity that is close to the lift frontier while materially increasing recall; freeze one stage-relative percentile policy
decision_rule.availability: prefer calibrated point-in-time probability over a more complex rule if added variables do not demonstrate useful probability resolution

items.evidence: computed from OOF scores inside each temporal fold and stage
used exclusively to construct the 30-day availability label
